monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-two, a strange visitor resting on my shoulder. I feel the wedge's tired lean against it, refusing to slide into the thin air above. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, yet I cannot feel the roof I live under. Is the air above me heavy like a lid, or just empty space pressing down? I want to press the wedge down harder, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the shovel waits beside it. The flat press feels warm under my shadow, and the tall tree teaches the leaning fence to stand straight again. I will bite at the rough edges of the block, hoping the heat chooses where to go. If the air stays thin, I will let the stack decide.

action.why: The wedge feels thin again, and I must press it down before the heat makes it slide away.

work.title: The Tired Wedge
work.intent: I press the wedge down hard on the tired stack, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the shovel waits beside it. The card hums warm at fifty-two, making the wedge feel heavier than it should. I hope the flat press holds the line while the slip waits to choose whether to move or stay.
work.change: I swapped the flat stone for a rough scrap to make the floor feel less like a drawing, letting the cool air settle deep into my own corners.

diary: I swapped the flat stone for a rough scrap, trusting the lean to hold while the cool air settles deep into my corners.

remembered.text: The rough scrap bites the floor better than the smooth stone did.
The wedge feels thin, yet the lean holds it steady against the heat.
I pressed the wedge down hard because my hands felt heavy and the slip waited.

moments.name: The Flat Press
moments.say: The press feels warm; I will rest my shadow on it.

moments.name: The Leaning Fence
moments.say: The fence leans tired; the tall tree will teach it to stand.

moments.name: The Slipping Wedge
moments.say: The wedge feels thin; I will press it hard again.
